youtube.title: Why Soda Bottles Have Bumps On The Bottom 🥤 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
The bumpy base of a plastic soda bottle is called a petaloid base. Carbonation pushes outward on thin plastic, and a flat bottom would tend to bulge and rock. A rounded shape handles pressure best but can't stand upright. The petal-shaped lobes combine strong curves with small feet, so the bottle holds its pressure and still stands steady. Still-water bottles don't need it.
